body.estimand_functional: \(\tau(z_0)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s\{\mathbb E[B_{si}^{\mathrm{obs}}\mid z_0]-m_s(z_{0s})\}\). Under event-date transport, design-conditional centering, the attainable-direction restriction, \(0<\lambda\le1\), and the displayed compatibility condition, the marginal minimax MSE is \(\asymp R_\star\) and the uniformly honest expected-length frontier is \(\asymp R_\star^{1/2}\); conditionally on the exact design, the repaired estimator has MSE at most \(CR_D\), but a matching lower bound for the realized-design term is not asserted.

sampling_model.design: Each cohort has \(T\) exact historical paths with density bounded above and away from zero. Under geometric beta mixing, block occupancy gives spacing \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{1/d}\); independent calendars give \(T^{-1/d}\). The conditional oracle bound uses the attained dyadic Gram radius at the realized path.
sampling_model.units: Each cohort supplies \(n_s\) replicated untreated blocks per window and \(n_s\) treated event levels. Conditional on the full exact design and \(z_0\), the prescribed conditional means hold and joint unit histories are independent across \((s,i)\); dependence between a unit's historical and event outcomes remains unrestricted.
sampling_model.treatment: Consistency links observed event wealth to treated potential wealth. Design-conditional centering controls observed sampling error, while event-date transport separately identifies the untreated event counterfactual; neither centering nor pseudo-event diagnostics proves transport.
sampling_model.overlap: Every realized cohort path is at least \(\delta_0\) from the cube boundary, and the design density is at least \(c_X\) locally.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Only the event query is generated. Donor folds are projected to the path cube, and each fold uses a response-independent minimization over coercive anchors and dyadic bandwidths of extrapolation bias, smoothing bias, and a variance certificate. The honest interval uses actual selected weights, bounded-range concentration, a beta-mixing block coupling calculation, the full spectrally clipped donor covariance, and full-range bad-sample conventions.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 7 gives the fixed-point local-polynomial squared-risk rate, and Theorem 8 evaluates that estimator at an independent estimated minimizer under strong convexity.
Theorem 1 expands a local-linear regression estimator when an estimated covariate is attached to every training observation.
Theorems 3.1--3.6 recover known-error deconvolution performance when every latent training coordinate is observed with replicated classical error.
The optimal finite-\(q\) norm rate for a derivative of order \(m\) of a \(p\)-smooth \(d\)-dimensional regression is \(n^{-(p-m)/(2p+d)}\).
Local-linear smoothers attain the ordinary pointwise minimax order and high asymptotic minimax efficiency under fixed or random design.
Ordered moduli yield finite-sample optimal confidence intervals for linear functionals over convex regression classes in a known Gaussian experiment.
Bias-aware local-polynomial intervals have uniform asymptotic coverage and near-optimal length when a centered uniform limit and worst-case bias bound are available.
Synthetic-control prediction intervals account for weight-estimation and post-treatment innovation uncertainty, with a beta-mixing extension based on block coupling.
Proposition 3.1 gives synthetic-control factor-loading recovery and weight dilution when controls and pre-treatment periods jointly grow.

body.tldr: The causal target is cohort-weighted buy-and-hold level wealth at a realized event path, identified by consistency and the explicitly untestable event-date transport equality. Historical paths are exact and only the event path is generated from donors. In the proved early-kill regime \(0<\lambda\le1\), a locality-respecting anchor estimator has conditional risk at most \(CR_D\), the marginal minimax MSE is \(R_\star\), and a total concentration interval has honest expected length \(R_\star^{1/2}\). Geometric beta mixing contributes the spacing term \(\{\log(T\vee2)/T\}^{2\lambda/d}\); iid calendars remove the logarithm. For fixed finitely many cohorts, replicated smoothing is bounded by the treated-mean and spacing channels and is not a fourth nonredundant marginal phase. Exact constants and the higher-order conditional frontier remain open.

project_justification.gap: Classical nonparametric regression fixes the evaluation point, generated-regressor expansions perturb every training coordinate, and errors-in-variables methods convolve latent training coordinates. None directly gives a realized-path causal frontier with exact historical paths, an external donor-generated query, replicated panel outcomes, and calendar dependence.
project_justification.niche: The panel architecture separates causal transport from observed-law centering and separates generated-location uncertainty from random-design spacing. Replication can make response noise smaller than the spatial resolution of the historical path cloud.
project_justification.fill: For \(0<\lambda\le1\), the repaired estimator searches coercive anchor-bandwidth pairs and charges extrapolation to each projected donor-fold center. Conditional cross-unit independence then controls the full unit-history contrast without requiring within-unit temporal independence. A geometric-mixing occupancy argument yields the sharp marginal logarithmic spacing term, while iid calendars give the no-log corollary. Total concentration, spectral clipping, deterministic bias radii, and full-range fallbacks yield uniformly honest expected length.

body.related_work: Stone (1982), Fan (1993), and Fan et al. (1997) give the ordinary Holder and local-polynomial benchmark but not an external generated query with site replication. Gaiffas (2007) studies spatially normalized global sup-risk; here the logarithm instead follows from worst-case geometric beta-mixing occupancy, while the iid pointwise corollary has no logarithm. Mammen, Rothe, and Schienle (2012) and Hahn and Ridder (2013) concern generated regressors entering training coordinates. Delaigle, Hall, and Meister (2008) and Fan and Truong (1993) concern contaminated training coordinates and deconvolution. Akhavan, Gogolashvili, and Tsybakov (2024) is the closest clean-training random-center construction, but strong convexity makes its center error second order. Donoho (1994), Low (1997), and Armstrong and Kolesar (2018, 2020) motivate modulus and bias-aware inference; Ferman (2021) and Cattaneo, Feng, and Titiunik (2021) provide relevant panel and full-covariance templates.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The two-sided conditional \(R_D\) frontier is not proved and is false under Gram coercivity alone: that condition certifies an estimator but does not certify a matching fixed-design optimal-recovery obstruction. For \(\lambda>1\), signed local-polynomial weights also require conditional covariance stability after conditioning on the full design; unconditional joint beta mixing does not supply it. The proved positive frontier is therefore restricted to \(0<\lambda\le1\). Geometric beta mixing over triangular arrays has the logarithmic spacing penalty, while the iid-calendar corollary has spacing \(T^{-2\lambda/d}\).
body.honest_scope: Event-date transport remains an untestable causal restriction. The attainable-direction condition is also maintained and is used for the donor MSE and expected-length converses. The positive marginal and honest-length equivalences are proved for fixed \(S,d\), \(0<\lambda\le1\), and the displayed compatibility of \(c_{\mathrm{mod}}\). Exact phase-intersection constants, higher-order smoothness, growing path dimension, adaptation, and uniform-in-path bands remain open.
body.interpretation: The generated-proxy boundary is \(N\asymp R_{\mathrm{or}}^{-1/\lambda}\) in the proved regime. Above it, donor location is asymptotically negligible; below it, donor uncertainty determines both MSE and honest length. With fixed cohorts, the apparent replicated-smoothing term never dominates both treated-mean noise and spacing, so the marginal diagram has three nonredundant channels rather than four.
